newsitem.title: UK: European veg oils end quiet session little changed.
newsitem.headline: European veg oils end quiet session little changed.

text.p: European vegetable oil prices finished a quiet session little changed on Thursday with trading affected by the Thanksgiving day holiday in the U.S. and a trade dinner in Hamburg.
News that Pakistan had bought 6,000 tonnes of RBD palm oil at $545.9 a tonne c and f for shipment by Decmber 31 had little impact on the market.
Crude palm oil closed unchanged and tradeless despite rumours about the "MV Antea" which are still circulating.
The vessel is due to berth on Friday at Port Klang in Malaysia at around 0200 gmt.
Traders said there was some talk that the problems with the "Antea" went beyond contamination of its tanks.

"We are hearing all sorts of rumours about this vessel. But none have been confirmed and most people are treating them with a certain amount of caution, because it is not beyond the bounds of possibility that someone, somewhere is trying to make a fast buck out of this," said a trader.
Refined palm oil closed mixed with RBD oil $2.50 up and olein $2.50 down with no further business reported during the afternoon.
Coconut oil closed around $5 up after Nov/Dec traded at $810 a tonne cif.
Palmkernel oil was mixed at $5 up to $5 down in a tradeless market.
In a tradeless soft oils sector soy oil closed 0.50 guilders up while rape oil was 0.50 guilders higher to unchanged.
Based on sellers' prices, the premium for rape oil over soyoil was 1.50 to 4.50 guilders at the close against 1.50 to 4.50 guilders on Wednesday.
